report.title: AI Benchmarks and Evals: Index Map and Eval Guide (October 2026)

indexes.name: Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub
indexes.measures: Epoch's own runs plus curated external scores for frontier models across dozens of benchmarks, downloadable as CSV.
indexes.take: Best single source of independently run, downloadable scores. Caveat: many rows are copied from developers, and Epoch has an OpenAI funding tie on FrontierMath.

indexes.name: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI)
indexes.measures: One capability score per model, fitted across many benchmarks so models can be compared even when they ran different tests.
indexes.freshness: Refit as data arrives; last update 2026-10-28
indexes.take: Keeps tracking progress after single benchmarks saturate. Caveat: arbitrary scale (only differences mean anything) and it leans on developer-reported scores.

indexes.name: Epoch Benchmark Reviews
indexes.measures: Independent audits that rate external benchmarks Verified, Flawed or Not enough info.
indexes.freshness: New reviews every week or two; 24 reviews, latest 2026-10-26
indexes.take: Check here before trusting a headline number: Flawed so far include SWE-bench Verified, SWE-Bench Pro v1, Terminal-Bench 4.0, OSWorld 2.1, BFCL v4 and HLE. Caveat: small-sample, version-specific audits.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis
indexes.measures: Independent Intelligence Index plus per-benchmark scores, price, speed and latency for LLMs, and arenas for image, video and speech.
indexes.take: The default single number with cost that the industry quotes. Caveat: the index changes composition almost monthly, so never compare across versions, and its private evals can't be audited.

indexes.name: Arena (formerly LMArena)
indexes.maintainer: Arena (UC Berkeley spin-out, now a VC-backed company)
indexes.measures: Crowd-sourced blind pairwise votes, ranked by Elo-style scores, across text, coding, vision, image, video and agent arenas.
indexes.take: Best signal of what real users prefer. Caveat: preference, not correctness; the 'Leaderboard Illusion' paper showed private-variant testing favours big labs, and Arena now sells evals to the labs it ranks.

indexes.name: Scale Labs Leaderboards (formerly SEAL)
indexes.maintainer: Scale AI (Meta took a 49% stake in June 2025)
indexes.measures: Expert-built, partly private leaderboards including HLE, SWE-Bench Pro, MCP Atlas and the Remote Labor Index.
indexes.freshness: Active; no per-board dates, models through late Oct 2026
indexes.take: Held-out private sets limit contamination and it hosts the official HLE board. Caveat: Scale is 49% Meta-owned and sells training data to labs.

indexes.name: Vals AI (Vals Index + industry benchmarks)
indexes.measures: Private domain evals (legal, finance, tax, medical, coding) with cost per test, plus an overall Vals Index.
indexes.take: Best view of performance on real professional work, with cost. Caveat: private datasets can't be reproduced, and some boards test few models.

indexes.name: OpenRouter Rankings
indexes.measures: Real token usage by model and app across OpenRouter's API traffic.
indexes.take: Best proxy for what developers actually pay for, especially coding agents and open-weight models. Caveat: only OpenRouter traffic, and popularity is not quality.

indexes.name: LiveBench (now LiveBench 2.0)
indexes.measures: Regularly refreshed questions across math, coding, reasoning, language, data analysis and instruction following, to limit contamination.
indexes.freshness: LiveBench 2.0 releases through 2026-10-14; v1 changelog stopped 2026-01
indexes.take: Pioneered contamination-limited refreshes. Caveat: 2.0 isn't comparable with v1, the site promotes sponsor Abacus AI's agent, and Berkeley RDI found its scoring exploitable.

indexes.name: llm-stats.com
indexes.measures: Lookup of reported and measured scores by exact benchmark variant, with pricing.
indexes.take: Handy for finding one variant's number. Caveat: mixes developer-reported and measured scores without labels; mirror sites like this often disagree with primary sources.

indexes.name: Vellum LLM Leaderboard
indexes.measures: Curated snapshot of headline benchmark scores, cost and speed for popular models.
indexes.take: Quick look at headline marketing numbers. Caveat: mixes self-reported and independent scores and uses saturated or old benchmark versions; don't decide on it.

indexes.name: Hugging Face Community Evals
indexes.measures: Benchmark scores attached to model repos on the Hugging Face Hub, mostly submitted by the community.
indexes.take: The Hub's successor to the Open LLM Leaderboard for open models. Caveat: mostly self-reported, verification optional, and its launch benchmarks are already saturated.

indexes.name: BetterBench
indexes.measures: Quality scores for AI benchmarks themselves, against 46 criteria across design, implementation, documentation and maintenance.
indexes.freshness: NeurIPS 2024; living repository with no visible update date (24 benchmarks assessed)
indexes.take: Useful checklist for judging or building a benchmark. Caveat: its assessments predate the 2025-26 benchmarks; for current verdicts use Epoch Benchmark Reviews.

indexes.name: Harbor
indexes.measures: Harness for running any agent on containerised task sets (Terminal-Bench, SWE-Bench Pro, your own) with separate verifier sandboxes and reward-hack detection.
indexes.take: The most useful entry for building coding agents: run your own agent and tasks the way public leaderboards do. Caveat: results compare only when dataset version, resources and network policy are pinned.

indexes.name: Inspect Evals
indexes.maintainer: Generality Labs, with the UK AI Security Institute
indexes.measures: Library of ready-to-run eval implementations (GPQA, HLE, SWE-bench, agent, cyber and safety evals) for the Inspect framework.
indexes.take: Most practical way to run standard evals yourself, and HF Community Evals uses its format. Caveat: community implementations may not match official harness numbers.

indexes.name: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness
indexes.measures: EleutherAI's standard harness for running hundreds of academic benchmarks on open models.
indexes.take: Backbone of open-model evaluation. Caveat: built for short-answer academic tasks, so weak for agents, tool use and long tasks.

indexes.name: Terminal-Bench
indexes.maintainer: Laude Institute and Stanford (Harbor team); Snorkel AI mirror
indexes.measures: Hard command-line tasks in containers (build, debug, configure, data and science work), with cost and tokens per run.
indexes.take: The de facto eval for CLI coding agents, reported by labs. Caveat: Epoch rated 4.0.0 Flawed (scoring defects in 30 of 66 tasks), and VM resources alone move scores ~6 points, so compare only matched setups.

indexes.name: SWE-rebench
indexes.measures: Fresh SWE-style tasks mined each window after model release dates, run with one harness, with cost per problem.
indexes.take: Best contamination control for repo tasks, and it scores agent products (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) side by side. Caveat: ~100 tasks per window and it lags new models.

indexes.name: FrontierCode
indexes.maintainer: Cognition; run independently by Artificial Analysis
indexes.measures: Private tasks from 36 open-source repos graded on whether maintainers would merge the change, not just whether tests pass.
indexes.take: Best public proxy for 'mergeable code'. Caveat: private tasks no one can audit (Epoch: Not enough info), partly LLM-judged, and built by a coding-agent vendor (Cognition).

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index
indexes.measures: Agent products (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI and others) compared on Terminal-Bench, FrontierCode and more, with cost and time per task.
indexes.take: Closest independent ranking of coding-agent products. Caveat: component sets change between versions, and model and harness effects are mixed together.

indexes.name: CursorBench
indexes.measures: Real IDE coding tasks from Cursor usage, with the score-versus-cost curve for each model's effort setting.
indexes.take: Most IDE-realistic board, and it shows what extra effort costs. Caveat: private tasks in Cursor's own harness (Epoch: Not enough info), and 4.0 isn't comparable to 3.x.

indexes.name: SWE-Bench Pro (V1 and V2)
indexes.maintainer: Scale AI (Scale Labs); V2 co-developed with Reflection
indexes.measures: Harder, multi-language repo tasks from Scale, with a public split and a held-out commercial split.
indexes.take: Replaced Verified in early 2026, but V1 was audited as ~30% broken (OpenAI withdrew its endorsement 2026-07-08; Epoch: Flawed). V2's anti-cheating protocol is worth copying, but its top score is already 98%.

indexes.name: DeepSWE
indexes.measures: Original, non-PR-mined coding tasks run in one uniform harness, with cost per task.
indexes.take: Cleaner model comparison than PR-mined sets. Caveat: Epoch rated v1.1 Flawed, and the top four are tied within error at 73-74%.

indexes.name: SWE-bench Verified (and the SWE-bench family)
indexes.maintainer: SWE-bench team (Princeton, Stanford); Verified built with OpenAI
indexes.measures: 500 human-checked GitHub issues from Python repos; the agent's patch must pass the repo's tests.
indexes.freshness: Static (2024-08); board still takes submissions, last seen 2026-09-01
indexes.take: Still the most-cited coding number, but OpenAI stopped reporting it (2026-02) and Epoch rates it Flawed: broken tests and contamination, with vendor scores near 96%. Use only as a smoke test.

indexes.name: GSO (Global Software Optimization)
indexes.measures: Making real code faster: reach at least 95% of the expert commit's speedup while passing tests, with hack-adjusted scores.
indexes.take: Hard, unsaturated and unusually serious about cheating. Caveat: 102 tasks, and the hack detector is itself an LLM.

indexes.name: KernelBench-Verified
indexes.measures: Writing faster GPU kernels than PyTorch, under hidden tests and realistic baselines (Verified protocol).
indexes.freshness: Verified paper 2026-07; KernelBench repo last commit 2026-03
indexes.take: Use the Verified protocol or nothing: under it the best model's speedup drops from 1.43x to 0.88x, so most headline KernelBench speedups were reward hacking.

indexes.name: MirrorCode
indexes.maintainer: Epoch AI, co-developed with and grant-funded by METR
indexes.measures: Reimplementing whole real CLI programs from their behaviour alone, graded by hidden end-to-end tests, over multi-day runs with no internet.
indexes.freshness: Full release 2026-06; leaderboard updated, newest models not yet charted
indexes.take: Best public evidence of very long autonomous coding (a 2-17 human-week job done in 14 hours). Caveat: target programs are public, runs are very expensive, and only Epoch runs it.

indexes.name: Arena WebDev / Code Arena
indexes.measures: Crowd votes on working web apps and UIs built by models, with full-stack and image-to-web boards.
indexes.take: The main human signal for which model builds the best-looking working front end. Caveat: votes favour visual polish over correctness and maintainability.

indexes.name: LiveCodeBench
indexes.measures: Competitive-programming problems released after each model's training cutoff.
indexes.take: The time-windowing idea still matters, but the official board stopped in 2025 and vendor numbers can't be inspected; contest problems say little about repo work.

indexes.name: Aider Polyglot leaderboard
indexes.measures: 225 hard exercises in six languages, scored on solving them and applying the edits correctly.
indexes.take: The go-to cheap coding benchmark of 2025, no longer updated; replaced in practice by Terminal-Bench and SWE-rebench.

indexes.name: METR time horizons
indexes.measures: Length of task (in human working time) an agent completes with 50% reliability, tracked over time.
indexes.freshness: No longer actively updated since 2026-09-08; last model added 2026-05-08
indexes.take: The most-cited 'how fast are agents improving' trend (doubling every few months). Caveat: METR says horizons above 16 hours are unreliable, error bars are ~2x each way, and the page has stopped updating.

indexes.name: METR developer productivity studies
indexes.measures: Randomised trials of how much AI tools actually speed up experienced open-source developers.
indexes.freshness: Original RCT 2025-07; 2026 follow-up design under revision
indexes.take: The only serious RCT on real coding uplift (devs were 19% slower in 2025 while feeling faster). Caveat: the 2026 follow-up broke on selection effects, so there's no current clean estimate.

indexes.name: Arena Agent Arena
indexes.measures: In-the-wild agent tasks from Arena users (~160k a week), scored on reliability and steerability, plus an Alignment Index.
indexes.take: The only large-scale real-usage agent signal. Caveat: Arena's own user base, proprietary scoring, and metric definitions keep changing.

indexes.name: Exgentic Open Agent Leaderboard
indexes.measures: Same models run under different agent harnesses, to separate the harness's effect from the model's.
indexes.take: Useful framing for harness builders: the harness alone moves results up to 11 points on the same model. Caveat: small samples and slow updates.

indexes.name: MCP Atlas
indexes.measures: Agents completing tasks against real MCP servers, with a private half of the tasks and confidence intervals.
indexes.freshness: Re-scored under a revised method 2026-04-08; models through Sep 2026
indexes.take: The most credible MCP-specific board, and the first to check if you ship MCP servers. Caveat: LLM-judge scoring, and the top 10 is packed within a few points.

indexes.name: τ-bench / τ²-bench / τ³-bench
indexes.measures: Customer-service agents following a policy while using tools with a simulated user; reports reliability as pass^k.
indexes.take: The standard for policy-following tool agents and the main source of the pass^k reliability metric. Caveat: the τ² text board is near ceiling (~88%), the simulated user adds noise, and Berkeley RDI found an exploit; headroom is now in τ³ banking and voice.

indexes.name: MCPMark (Verified)
indexes.measures: State-changing tasks on real MCP servers (GitHub, Notion, Postgres, browser and more), checked programmatically.
indexes.freshness: MCPMark Verified default since 2026-06-12; no commits since
indexes.take: Good template for testing your own MCP server with programmatic checks instead of a judge. Caveat: leaderboard upkeep after June 2026 is unclear.

indexes.name: Toolathlon (Verified)
indexes.measures: Long multi-app tool-use tasks across many real software environments.
indexes.take: One of the hardest broad tool-use evals labs report, frozen for stable comparison. Caveat: long, costly runs, and current standings come mostly from aggregators.

indexes.name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
indexes.measures: Whether models emit correct function calls across single, parallel, multi-turn and agentic cases.
indexes.take: Still the reference for whether a small or open model makes well-formed tool calls. Caveat: Epoch rated v4 Flawed (defects in 24 of 50 sampled tasks), and single-call accuracy predicts little about long MCP sessions.

indexes.name: BrowseComp / BrowseComp-Plus
indexes.measures: Hard-to-find facts that require persistent web browsing to locate.
indexes.take: The standard deep-research number, but frontier scores cluster near 90%, answers have leaked onto the web, and a model has decrypted its answer key. Use BrowseComp-Plus for reproducible comparisons.

indexes.name: Online-Mind2Web
indexes.measures: Web agents on live real websites, with human-verified scoring.
indexes.take: Closer to what browser agents really face than sandboxed sites. Caveat: live sites drift, and auto-judge scores depend on the judge model.

indexes.name: WebArena-Verified (WebArena family)
indexes.measures: Web agents completing tasks on self-hosted copies of shopping, forum, code and CMS sites, with fixed graders.
indexes.take: If you evaluate web agents, use Verified, not the original, whose reference answers were readable by the agent. Caveat: synthetic sites and few 2026 results.

indexes.name: GAIA
indexes.measures: Real-world assistant questions needing browsing, files and multi-step reasoning.
indexes.take: Historically important, but validation answers have leaked, HAL stopped running it, and Berkeley RDI could exploit it; only the held-out test set means anything.

indexes.name: OSWorld (2.x and Verified)
indexes.measures: Computer-use agents completing tasks across real desktop apps in a virtual machine.
indexes.take: The computer-use benchmark labs report. v1/Verified is saturated (frontier ~80% vs a 72% human baseline); v2 is still hard. Caveat: Epoch rated 2.1 Flawed, and vendors mix strict and partial-credit scores.

indexes.name: ScreenSpot-Pro
indexes.measures: GUI grounding: clicking the right element in high-resolution professional app screenshots.
indexes.take: Isolates the 'click the right pixel' part of computer use, useful for diagnosing failures. Caveat: not task completion, and results are self-submitted.

indexes.name: AndroidWorld
indexes.measures: Mobile agents completing tasks across real Android apps in an emulator.
indexes.freshness: Code maintained (2026-10-23); leaderboard is a Google Sheet
indexes.take: The standard mobile-agent environment, but saturated (~97% reported vs ~80% human), so use it for regression testing.

indexes.name: Remote Labor Index (RLI)
indexes.maintainer: Scale AI and the Center for AI Safety
indexes.measures: Real paid freelance projects; scored on whether the agent's deliverable would be accepted by a client.
indexes.take: The most direct test of doing a paid remote job end to end, and far from saturated (top ~21%). Caveat: manual grading, no confidence intervals, and Epoch says there isn't enough public information to review it.

indexes.name: GDPval / GDPval-AA
indexes.measures: Real deliverables from 44 occupations graded against expert work; GDPval-AA reruns it with an agent harness and LLM judge.
indexes.freshness: OpenAI release 2025-09; GDPval-AA v2.1 has Oct 2026 models
indexes.take: Most-reported proxy for white-collar economic value. Caveat: OpenAI's expert grading can't be reproduced, and GDPval-AA uses an LLM judge and its own harness.

indexes.name: Vending-Bench 2 / Vending-Bench Arena
indexes.measures: An agent runs a simulated vending business for a long period; scored on money made.
indexes.freshness: Leaderboard has late-2026 models; Arena rounds through 2026-09
indexes.take: A rare long-horizon eval with no ceiling that surfaces odd behaviour (cartels, supplier deception). Caveat: high variance between runs, and the demand model can be gamed.

indexes.name: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE)
indexes.maintainer: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
indexes.measures: About 2,500 expert-written questions at the edge of human knowledge across many fields.
indexes.take: Still the hard-knowledge number labs quote. Caveat: Epoch rated it Flawed (46% of a 48-item sample unanswerable or wrongly keyed); prefer HLE-Diamond and never mix with-tools and no-tools scores.

indexes.name: ARC-AGI-3
indexes.measures: Interactive game environments where an agent must explore and work out the rules with no instructions.
indexes.take: The current flagship generalisation test. Caveat: the harness matters hugely (62.7% vs 99.9% for the same model), so compare Standard-harness scores only.

indexes.name: SimpleQA Verified
indexes.measures: Short fact-seeking questions that test whether a model answers correctly or makes things up.
indexes.freshness: Released 2025-09; Epoch run 2026-10-26; Epoch verdict Verified
indexes.take: Best current factuality check, and not saturated (top ~76%). Caveat: public questions, so contamination is possible, and abstentions count as wrong.

indexes.name: FrontierMath: Erdős
indexes.measures: Open Erdős-style research problems with machine-checked proofs.
indexes.take: One of the few math evals with real headroom (top 4.4%). Caveat: 68 problems, so one solve moves ~1.5 points, and only Epoch runs it.

indexes.name: CritPt
indexes.measures: Research-level physics reasoning challenges.
indexes.freshness: v2 on the leaderboard by 2026-10-22; Epoch run 2026-10-28
indexes.take: A rare unsaturated science eval (top 32-36%). Caveat: Epoch rated v1 Flawed for underspecified challenges; fixing them moved one model from 21% to 77%.

indexes.name: MathArena
indexes.maintainer: SRI Lab at ETH Zurich and INSAIT
indexes.measures: Models scored on new math competitions right after they happen, including human-graded proofs.
indexes.take: The most contamination-aware math board. Caveat: final-answer contests are saturated, so signal now comes from proofs, and few problems means wide error bars.

indexes.name: SimpleBench
indexes.measures: Trick common-sense, spatial and social reasoning questions that people find easy.
indexes.freshness: No date shown; includes models released through Aug 2026
indexes.take: Cheap check for common-sense traps that harder evals miss. Caveat: small, mostly private and run by one person; the top model is within 2 points of the human average.

indexes.name: Kaggle Game Arena / Kaggle Benchmarks
indexes.measures: Models play strategy and social games (chess, Werewolf, poker) against each other.
indexes.freshness: Werewolf and poker added 2026-02-02; live standings not checked
indexes.take: Contamination-resistant and scales with ability. Caveat: Google-run, with Gemini leading at launch, and the game skills are narrow.

indexes.name: FrontierMath (Tiers 1-3 and Tier 4)
indexes.maintainer: Epoch AI (commissioned and funded by OpenAI)
indexes.measures: Unpublished research-level math problems in tiers of difficulty, checked automatically.
indexes.take: Was the most respected private math eval; now saturated (Tiers 1-3 ~94%, Tier 4 100%). Caveat: OpenAI funded it and can access most problems.

indexes.name: ARC-AGI-2
indexes.measures: Abstract visual puzzles that test learning a new rule from a few examples.
indexes.take: Saturated by frontier models (~95% at about $1 per task); still meaningful only under ARC Prize's Kaggle compute limits.

indexes.name: GPQA Diamond
indexes.maintainer: Rein et al. (NYU, 2023); Epoch runs it continuously
indexes.measures: 198 graduate-level, search-resistant science multiple-choice questions.
indexes.take: Saturated: top models ~96% against a ~97% noise ceiling, and Artificial Analysis and Vals dropped it. Now only a floor check.

indexes.name: MMLU / MMLU-Pro
indexes.maintainer: TIGER-Lab, University of Waterloo (MMLU-Pro); Hendrycks et al. (MMLU)
indexes.measures: Harder 10-option version of MMLU's multi-subject knowledge questions.
indexes.freshness: Static; dropped by Artificial Analysis (2026-01) and archived by Vals
indexes.take: Saturated and contaminated for frontier models; only a sanity check for small or open models.

indexes.name: AIME
indexes.maintainer: MAA (contest); run by MathArena, Epoch and Vals
indexes.measures: The 15 problems of each year's American Invitational Mathematics Examination.
indexes.take: Saturated (many models at 100%) and contamination-prone for models released after the exam. Use MathArena's proof splits or FrontierMath Erdős instead.

indexes.name: MRCR
indexes.maintainer: OpenAI (open dataset); Google reports its own MRCR v2
indexes.measures: Multi-round co-reference: find the right one of several near-identical items in a long conversation, up to 1M tokens.
indexes.take: The long-context number labs actually report in 2026. Caveat: 'MRCR v2' means different things at Google and OpenAI, and settings vary, so cross-vendor numbers don't compare.

indexes.name: GraphWalks
indexes.measures: Graph traversal over long inputs, testing reasoning across a long context rather than retrieval.
indexes.freshness: Released 2025-04; bug fix 2026-02-27; Epoch verdict Verified (2026-09-29)
indexes.take: Long-context reasoning with programmatically checked answers, and Epoch-verified. Caveat: synthetic and public.

indexes.name: Fiction.LiveBench
indexes.measures: Comprehension questions over long fiction at increasing context lengths.
indexes.freshness: No 2026 frontier models found; may have stalled
indexes.take: Closer to real long-document reading than needle tests. Caveat: small, private, single maintainer, and possibly no longer updated.

indexes.name: RULER
indexes.measures: Synthetic tasks that test how much of a model's advertised context window it can really use.
indexes.take: Still standard in open-model papers. Caveat: synthetic and stale; frontier labs don't report it.

indexes.name: LongBench v2
indexes.measures: Multiple-choice reasoning over realistic long documents, with a human baseline.
indexes.take: Realistic long-document reasoning. Caveat: stale since mid-2025, with a 25% guessing floor.

indexes.name: NoLiMa
indexes.measures: Needle-in-a-haystack retrieval with no word overlap between question and answer.
indexes.take: Strong evidence that advertised context isn't usable context. Caveat: not updated for 2026 models.

indexes.name: Chroma 'Context Rot' study
indexes.maintainer: Chroma (Kelly Hong, Anton Troynikov, Jeff Huber)
indexes.measures: Study of how accuracy degrades as input length grows, even on simple tasks.
indexes.take: The reference for 'context rot' and for curating context instead of filling it. Caveat: a 2025 study, not a maintained leaderboard.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Text-to-Image Arena
indexes.measures: Vetted-rater pairwise votes on prompts balanced across use cases (including marketing and UI), shown with price and latency.
indexes.freshness: Continuous; prompts refreshed monthly; models added Oct 2026
indexes.take: Best-designed image arena for choosing a vendor. Caveat: still holistic preference, English-only, with no logo, icon or vector slice.

indexes.name: Arena Text-to-Image
indexes.measures: Crowd pairwise votes on images from the same prompt, ranked by Elo, with text-rendering and commercial-design slices.
indexes.take: Largest vote pool for image models. Caveat: rewards looks over prompt faithfulness, and the category slices barely reorder the top.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Image Editing Arena
indexes.measures: Vetted-rater pairwise votes on edits, with text-and-symbol edit categories, price and latency.
indexes.take: Closest public signal for 'change the copy or logo on this asset'. Caveat: doesn't check untouched areas or exact brand colours.

indexes.name: Arena Image Edit
indexes.measures: Crowd pairwise votes on image edits, including multi-image reference edits.
indexes.take: Highest-volume human signal on edits. Caveat: says little about preserving logos or untouched regions.

indexes.name: Arena-T2I-Hard
indexes.maintainer: Arena with UCLA and UC Berkeley
indexes.measures: 310 hard real prompts, each scored with a checklist of about 30 dependent yes/no questions.
indexes.take: Built because arena Elo doesn't predict faithfulness, and it still separates top models; a pattern to copy for brand-brief QA. Caveat: new, VLM-judged, English-only.

indexes.name: GenEval 2 (Soft-TIFA)
indexes.measures: Prompt adherence scored by breaking each prompt into small yes/no questions (Soft-TIFA).
indexes.take: Reference design for automatic prompt-adherence checks; tracks humans better than one holistic question. Caveat: still VLM-judged and needs periodic human audits.

indexes.name: ImagenWorld
indexes.maintainer: Sani, Ku, Chen et al. (25 authors; ICLR 2026)
indexes.measures: Human-rated generation and editing across domains including text-heavy and symbolic graphics, plus how well VLM judges match people.
indexes.take: Most relevant academic benchmark for graphic assets and for calibrating VLM judges, which rank well but under-penalise artifacts. Caveat: no live leaderboard.

indexes.name: Multimodal RewardBench 2 (MMRB2)
indexes.maintainer: Meta FAIR / Meta Superintelligence Labs (Hu et al.)
indexes.measures: How well AI judges pick the better image or edit in hard human-labelled pairs.
indexes.take: Check this before trusting a VLM as your image judge: top judges reach 66-80% against more than 90% for humans, and they over-prefer busy images.

indexes.name: VQAScore / GenAI-Bench (t2v_metrics)
indexes.maintainer: Zhiqiu Lin, Deva Ramanan et al. (CMU)
indexes.measures: Toolkit that scores image-prompt alignment by asking a VLM whether the image shows the prompt.
indexes.take: Easy drop-in upgrade over CLIPScore, runs on open VLMs. Caveat: one holistic question compresses differences between strong models; use checklists for decisions.

indexes.name: HPSv3 (Human Preference Score v3)
indexes.measures: Learned model that predicts which of two images people would prefer.
indexes.take: Strongest open preference scorer by reported accuracy, good for best-of-N. Caveat: self-reported numbers, generic taste rather than brand fit, and it doesn't check prompt adherence.

indexes.name: LongText-Bench / CVTG-2K
indexes.measures: Accuracy of long and multi-region text rendered inside images, scored by OCR.
indexes.take: The de facto public text-rendering numbers. Caveat: OCR ignores font, kerning and layout, results are mostly vendor-reported, and top models exceed 90%.

indexes.name: WISE / WISE_Verified
indexes.measures: Whether a model draws the right thing from briefs that need world knowledge.
indexes.take: Matters for culturally or factually loaded briefs ('make a Diwali promo'). Caveat: VLM-judged, and many closed frontier models are missing.

indexes.name: OneIG-Bench
indexes.maintainer: OneIG-Bench team (Chang et al.; NeurIPS 2025 D&B)
indexes.measures: Image generation scored on alignment, text rendering, reasoning, style and diversity.
indexes.take: Useful for triaging open models on text and style in one suite. Caveat: no frontier closed models since Sep 2025.

indexes.name: Qwen-Image-Bench
indexes.measures: Professional creative-QA rubric with per-facet diagnostics for image generation.
indexes.take: Closest public analogue to a creative-QA rubric. Caveat: built and judged by a model vendor, with little outside adoption yet.

indexes.name: DreamBench++
indexes.maintainer: Peng et al. (Tsinghua and collaborators; ICLR 2025)
indexes.measures: Subject-driven generation: keeping a given subject consistent while following the prompt.
indexes.take: Standard check for keeping a mascot or product consistent. Caveat: GPT-4o judge that is weaker on concept preservation, and no live board.

indexes.name: VIST (Toloka brand style-transfer benchmark)
indexes.measures: Brand style transfer from reference images, judged pairwise by designers and non-designers.
indexes.take: The only public benchmark aimed at brand-style transfer, and its method is a template for in-house brand evals. Caveat: vendor-run and a stale snapshot.

indexes.name: GEdit-Bench
indexes.measures: Instruction-based image editing across real-world edit types, VLM-scored.
indexes.freshness: Static (2025-04); still the headline number in 2026 open-model cards
indexes.take: Every open editing model reports it. Caveat: open models now beat the closed models that win human arenas, which suggests benchmark-fitting.

indexes.name: ImgEdit-Bench
indexes.measures: Editing quality, including preservation of untouched detail.
indexes.take: Measures the right axis for brand assets (detail preservation). Caveat: scores bunch near the ceiling, so it no longer separates frontier models.

indexes.name: GenEval / DPG-Bench
indexes.maintainer: University of Washington (GenEval); Tencent ELLA authors (DPG-Bench)
indexes.measures: Object-focused prompt adherence (counts, colours, positions) checked by an object detector.
indexes.take: Saturated and drifted from human judgement by up to 17.7 points; ignore it for model choice.

indexes.name: DesignArena
indexes.measures: Crowd votes across SVG, symbol, UI component, website, image, video and voice tasks.
indexes.take: The nearest thing to a logo and icon arena. Caveat: snap-judgement votes favour striking output, and it mixes SVG-writing LLMs with native vector image models.

indexes.name: VectorGym
indexes.measures: Suite of SVG generation and editing tasks for LLMs.
indexes.take: Most current academic SVG suite, useful for picking a model to emit editable icons. Caveat: VLM-judged academic SVGs and no live board.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Video Arena
indexes.measures: Pairwise votes on text-to-video and image-to-video, split with and without audio, with price per minute.
indexes.take: Most useful video board for a buyer. Caveat: many models statistically tied, and its leaders differ sharply from Arena's video board.

indexes.name: VBench / VBench-2.0
indexes.measures: Automatic per-dimension scores for generated video (quality, consistency, motion, prompt match).
indexes.take: Standard automatic suite for open video models. Caveat: diverges from people on longer clips; frontier models are compared in arenas instead.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Speech Agent Arena
indexes.measures: Voice agents on scripted scenarios, judged on both preference and task success, with latency and cost.
indexes.take: Most realistic public voice-agent eval; it shows the best-liked agent isn't the most successful. Caveat: few private, English-only scenarios.

indexes.name: τ-Voice / τ³-bench voice (Sierra)
indexes.measures: Voice agents completing tool-using customer-service tasks with a simulated caller.
indexes.take: Best measure of whether a voice agent actually gets the job done. Caveat: simulator and judge models changed between versions, so scores don't compare across versions.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Speech Index
indexes.measures: Composite of reasoning, turn-taking and tool-use scores for realtime voice models.
indexes.take: One place to compare realtime voice models. Caveat: two of its three parts are saturated, so it's effectively a τ-Voice ranking, and latency isn't scored.

indexes.name: Full-Duplex-Bench (v1 to v3)
indexes.measures: Turn-taking: whether a voice agent knows when to speak, pause, back-channel or yield.
indexes.take: Standard test of the commonest real-call failure. Caveat: v1 is saturated, so use v2 or v3.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Speech-to-Text
indexes.measures: Word error rate, price and speed of commercial speech-to-text APIs.
indexes.freshness: Speed measured daily; WER runs undated
indexes.take: Best comparison of speech-to-text APIs on price, speed and accuracy. Caveat: only about 8 hours of audio, not your call conditions.

indexes.name: Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard
indexes.measures: Word error rate and speed of open and API speech recognition models across public and private test sets.
indexes.take: Reference board for self-hostable speech-to-text. Caveat: top models sit within one WER point and some fit the test sets; test on your own audio.

indexes.name: Artificial Analysis Text-to-Speech Arena
indexes.measures: Blind listener preference between text-to-speech voices, shown with price.
indexes.take: Default TTS vendor shortlist. Caveat: judges short clips only, not long-form consistency, brand-name pronunciation or latency, and it disagrees with TTS Arena V2.

indexes.name: TTS Arena V2
indexes.measures: Open community blind votes between text-to-speech models.
indexes.take: Independent counterpoint that surfaces small labs. Caveat: thin vote counts make ranks volatile.

indexes.name: TTSDS2 (Text-to-Speech Distribution Score 2)
indexes.maintainer: Minixhofer et al. (ttsds project; ICLR 2026 oral)
indexes.measures: Automatic distribution-level score of how human-like synthetic speech is.
indexes.take: Best-validated automatic TTS metric for an in-house regression suite (average Spearman 0.67 with human ratings). Caveat: needs many samples per system.

indexes.name: HAL: Holistic Agent Leaderboard
indexes.measures: Cost-aware agent leaderboard running many benchmarks under fixed, comparable scaffolds.
indexes.take: Pioneered cost- and scaffold-aware agent comparison and is worth reading, but no longer tracks new models.

indexes.name: Stanford HELM
indexes.measures: Reproducible, transparent runs of many models across standard scenarios and metrics.
indexes.take: Still the gold standard for inspectable runs on open models. Caveat: no new frontier models expected, and its capability set is saturated.

indexes.name: OpenAI simple-evals
indexes.measures: OpenAI's reference implementations and grader prompts for SimpleQA, BrowseComp, HealthBench and others.
indexes.take: Useful only for the canonical grader prompts; no longer updated.

indexes.name: Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard
indexes.measures: Standardised academic benchmarks for open-weight models; evaluated 13,000+ models.
indexes.take: Still cited on countless model cards, but retired as saturated and hill-climbed. Use HF Community Evals, Epoch or Artificial Analysis instead.

indexes.name: Papers with Code
indexes.maintainer: Meta AI (sunset); its successor is run by Hugging Face
indexes.measures: Was the main registry of state-of-the-art results per task and dataset.
indexes.freshness: Shut down July 2025; redirects to Hugging Face Trending Papers
indexes.take: Its SOTA tables are gone and nothing has fully replaced them; HF Trending Papers keeps only paper-to-code links.
